paper.paper_scope: The study evaluates how plastic deformation changes the elastic modulus of cold-rolled steel sheets (SPCE and SPCC), comparing macroscopic precision-tensile measurements before/after large deformation and after various pre-strain/heat-treatment/annealing conditions with microscopic nano-indentation measurements, in order to clarify the influence of the modulus change on spring-back.
paper.research_type: experimental (macroscopic precision tensile tests and nano-indentation), with supporting FEM simulation of spring-back
paper.title: Evaluation of change in material properties due to plastic deformation

unmapped_findings: The heat treatment used to recover the Cottrell atmosphere was 373 K for 90 h, chosen based on the average diffusion distance of solute C in an Fe matrix (D from X = (2Dt)^(1/2)).

The change in elastic modulus was used as input to an FEM simulation of spring-back after V-bending; using the varied (strain-dependent) modulus predicted spring-back more accurately than a constant initial elastic modulus.

Nano-indentation was performed with a spherical indenter tip (nominal radius R = 50 µm) instead of a Berkovich tip so that the indentation deforms the surface only elastically, following Hertz contact theory.
The elastic modulus near the grain boundary was found to be smaller than in the grain interior by nano-indentation, with values varying between grains of different orientation.

CMP treatment (after etching and Vickers-indentation marker placement) was applied to specimen surfaces before nano-indentation to remove the grain-boundary ditch formed by etching and reduce surface-roughness effects.
The nano-indentation apparatus (Triboscope, Hysitron Inc. mounted on a Shimadzu SPM-9500J2 AFM stage) and its force/displacement ranges and sensitivities are specified in Table 3.
